## Purpose

Implements the Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API proposed in #37003 on top of the merged KV-hints request envelope (#53423, RFC #53421): a `kv.retain` action lets an orchestrator that knows the workflow (an agent runtime, a router) tell vLLM which token ranges of a request's prompt it will reuse soon, so the prefix cache keeps them while the session waits on a tool call, instead of evicting them in pure LRU order.

This is a rewrite of the earlier revision of this PR, cut down to what the replay benchmarks validated: full-attention models only, one policy knob (the directive's priority), no sliding-window/Mamba handling, no measurement-only code. Seven commits, each reviewable on its own.

**Not a duplicate of**
- #59714 / RFC #59708 (@karen-sy): same envelope, a `vllm.set_priority` action executed by a scheduler-side dispatcher at request completion. That PR is a draft with the contract still open; this PR applies ranges in the block pool when blocks are cached and is meant to be aligned with that contract (action name/fields) once it lands. I will do the alignment on this PR.
- #47837: eviction order driven by the *scheduling* priority of requests, no per-range hints.
- #48704: retention policies for the tiered/offloaded store, not the GPU prefix cache.

## Design

Wire format (top-level `kv_hints` on `/v1/chat/completions`, validated with a 400 on malformed input):

```json
{"kv_hints": {"protocol_version": "0.1", "message_id": "t1",
  "actions": [{"action_id": "t1:retain", "action_type": "kv.retain", "action_version": "1.0",
    "payload": {"scope": "session-id", "directives": [
      {"start": 0,    "end": 1200, "priority": 80, "duration": 86410},
      {"start": 1200, "end": null, "priority": 40, "duration": 86410}]}}]}}
```

- A directive protects the token range `[start, end)` of the prompt (`end: null` = to the end of the prompt, `covers_output: true` = the generated tail) with a priority 1–100 for `duration` seconds; priority 0 releases. Priorities must be non-increasing along the token axis (a later block is useless without its prefix).
- Protection is **soft**: the LRU free list is drained first, then protected blocks go lowest priority first; an expired protection is demoted to the LRU tail, not evicted. Hinted requests change the eviction *order*, never the capacity.
- A block keeps one hold per `scope` and is protected at the strongest hold; a scope only edits its own hold. `scope` is not authenticated (see `docs/usage/security.md`).
- With no hints the pool runs the upstream LRU path: retention bookkeeping starts with the first `kv.retain` of the process.

Commits:
1. `[Core] Add the kv.retain KV-hint action schema and parser` — `vllm/v1/kv_hints/retain.py`, strict (frontend) / lenient (engine) parsing, caps on actions and directives.
2. `[Frontend] Accept a kv_hints envelope on chat completions` — `ChatCompletionRequest.kv_hints`, validated, forwarded as request metadata; security note.
3. `[V1][Core] Priority-based KV-cache eviction driven by kv.retain hints` — `PriorityEvictionQueue` sidecar (lazy heap, expiry index) wired into `BlockPool`.
4. `[V1][Core] Drop a stale free copy when its hash is cached again` — an unreachable old copy no longer sits protected.
5. `[V1][Core] Keep one retention hold per scope and protect at the maximum` — per-scope holds; a scope lowering a block lowers its holds below it; orphaned descendants are reaped when the last copy of a hash leaves.
6. `[V1][Core] Link blocks into the hash chain only for full-attention KV groups` — the chain rules assume a lookup walks the chain from the first block; sliding-window and Mamba groups are left alone (keeps `test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector` green).
7. `[V1][Core] Keep the hint-free path at upstream cost until the first kv.retain hint` — see the microbenchmark below.

Out of scope here: hybrid/sliding-window specific retention (a follow-up), gRPC/Responses endpoints.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_hints tests/v1/core/test_priority_eviction.py \
       tests/tool_use/test_chat_completion_request_validations.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       "tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector" -q
pytest tests/v1/core -q          # CPU; compared against upstream/main in the same environment
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main..HEAD)
```

## Test Result

- 323 passed (the five suites above).
- `tests/v1/core` on a CPU-only box: the branch's failure set equals upstream/main's (read-only HF cache, no GPU: `test_kv_cache_utils` model-config downloads, `test_scheduler*` e2e). Before commit 6 the branch broke the two hybrid-Mamba cases; after it, none.
- pre-commit: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy 3.10, typos, SPDX).

## Evaluation

**What is compared.**

| column | server code | image | hints |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream LRU | upstream/main `189bbfb9` (the branch point; no retention code) | `base-189bbfb9-gfx90a` | none |
| branch LRU | this PR, commits 1–6 (`0b2ea132a6`, `0a6d417da9` after the rebase) | `base-0b2ea13-gfx90a` | none |
| branch + kv.retain | same code | same image | distance table |

Same client, session sets, KV size and send order in all three columns; the two LRU columns are byte-identical requests (no `retention_policy`). 2× MI250 (TP2), `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B`, ROCm images built from the commits above. Trace replay of agentic sessions with [inference-perf](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/inference-perf) (client changes: fixed send order, in-flight cap, `kv_hints` from a precomputed table — separate PR there), the model's live outputs substituted into later turns, a cold engine rollout before every arm, and the KV cache sized per set so that plain LRU hits 65–73 %. The table policy sends, per request, the priorities of a Belady-style distance table computed offline from one recorded run (next reuse of each block in the fixed send order); an event without a table entry sends no hint. Three 32-session sets drawn at random from the sessions of [`Exgentic/agent-llm-traces-v2`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Exgentic/agent-llm-traces-v2) (filters: ≥3 turns, largest request ≤20k tokens, no recorded output over 4096 tokens, sets disjoint; a draw is kept only if plain LRU at the KV floor is ≤73 %) — m32a/b/c: 461–510 requests, prompts ≈ 8k tokens, 3.6–4.2 M prompt tokens per set × in-flight 1/4/8/∞ = 12 arms per column. I found a case where `kv.retain` updates are skipped for reused cache blocks. I've attached a proposed fix with regression tests.

**Reproducer**

For FA with a block size of 16:

1. A request populates a 64-token cached prefix and sets a hold with `scope="owner"`, `priority=50`, and `duration=30`.
2. A second request has the same 64-token prefix plus 2 additional tokens, and sends `priority=0` for the same scope.
3. It reuses the 64 cached tokens but finishes without publishing another full block. The old holds remain instead of being released.

Setting, renewing, and lowering holds are affected as well. If the continuation publishes a new full block, the existing publication hook applies the hints, so whether the update takes effect depends on crossing a block boundary.

**Proposed fix**

Apply the request's hints to adopted local FA/MLA full-block cache hits after successful allocation. This reuses the existing retention handler, preserving scope handling, TTL calculation, and descendant handling.

Failed admission does not update holds, and ordinary decode steps do not trigger this additional update. The existing publication path remains unchanged. This does not extend retention support to SWA/Mamba or partial checkpoints.

**Tests**

The patch adds `TestRetentionOnAdoptedCacheHits` to `tests/v1/core/test_priority_eviction.py`, covering set/renew/lower/release, failed admission, and decode without repeated renewal.

With only these tests added to the original implementation, five fail and one passes; with the fix, all six pass. The 262 existing tests in `test_priority_eviction.py` and `test_prefix_caching.py` also pass on both implementations. These were isolated component test runs, not full CI or real-model serving validation.

The attached patch is against `92b4241b1493d682e01ebd857110ce98a7781e02`. Does applying hints when cached blocks are adopted match your intended semantics? Happy to open a PR against your branch if that would be easier to review.
[cache-hit-retention.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33668757/cache-hit-retention.patch)

I noticed another case while testing this PR.

Suppose session A caches 64 tokens and asks to retain them for 100 seconds. Shortly afterward, session B sends the same 64 tokens without any retention hints. With 16-token blocks, vLLM reuses the first 48 tokens and recomputes the last block to get logits.

When that new block is cached, `_drop_stale_copies` removes the old copy, including A’s hold. The new copy can still serve a cache hit, but A’s protection is gone even though it hasn’t expired. If B sends 65 tokens instead, it reuses all four original blocks and A’s holds remain.

It looks like the cleanup assumes a duplicate was recomputed because the old prefix chain was broken, but normal last-block recomputation can also trigger it.

I’ve attached a small patch that carries the old copy’s unexpired holds over to the replacement before removing it. It keeps their original expiry times, then lets the current request’s hints apply as usual, so an explicit downgrade or release still works.

Does that match what you intended? My assumption is that A wants to retain the cached content, regardless of which physical block holds it. If holds are intentionally tied to individual physical copies, this would change that behavior.

One thing this patch leaves open is concurrent updates from the same scope: an older request can publish after a newer one, so publication order doesn’t necessarily reflect the latest intent. I haven’t added revision tracking here; do you think that should be handled separately?

The patch includes 10 tests. Those and the 262 existing cache-component tests pass with the fix. I haven’t run real-model serving validation yet. This is separate from the earlier cache-hit fix and can be applied on its own.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces priority-based KV-cache eviction to vLLM, allowing specific blocks to be protected under memory pressure via retention directives. Key changes include the addition of a `PriorityEvictionQueue` (a min-heap with lazy TTL expiry), updates to `KVCacheBlock` to track priority metadata, and modifications to the `BlockPool` to handle prioritized allocation and freeing. The PR also extends the OpenAI chat completion protocol to support these directives. Review feedback identifies dead code regarding a fast-path flag, encapsulation issues where `BlockPool` accesses private queue members, and inconsistent state clearing when priority expires.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The flag `_has_prioritized_blocks` is initialized here, set in `_apply_retention_to_block` (line 556), and reset in `reset_prefix_cache` (line 612), but it is never read. The fast-path checks in `get_new_blocks` and `touch` use `self.priority_eviction_queue.num_blocks > 0` instead, which is more direct and accurate.

This flag and its associated logic are dead code and should be removed to improve clarity and maintainability. This includes the definition here and the assignments on lines 556 and 612.

detail.body:
## Purpose

Implements the Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API proposed in #37003 on top of the merged KV-hints request envelope (#53423, RFC #53421): a `kv.retain` action lets an orchestrator that knows the workflow (an agent runtime, a router) tell vLLM which token ranges of a request's prompt it will reuse soon, so the prefix cache keeps them while the session waits on a tool call, instead of evicting them in pure LRU order.

This is a rewrite of the earlier revision of this PR, cut down to what the replay benchmarks validated: full-attention models only, one policy knob (the directive's priority), no sliding-window/Mamba handling, no measurement-only code. Seven commits, each reviewable on its own.

**Not a duplicate of**
- #59714 / RFC #59708 (@karen-sy): same envelope, a `vllm.set_priority` action executed by a scheduler-side dispatcher at request completion. That PR is a draft with the contract still open; this PR applies ranges in the block pool when blocks are cached and is meant to be aligned with that contract (action name/fields) once it lands. I will do the alignment on this PR.
- #47837: eviction order driven by the *scheduling* priority of requests, no per-range hints.
- #48704: retention policies for the tiered/offloaded store, not the GPU prefix cache.

## Design

Wire format (top-level `kv_hints` on `/v1/chat/completions`, validated with a 400 on malformed input):

```json
{"kv_hints": {"protocol_version": "0.1", "message_id": "t1",
  "actions": [{"action_id": "t1:retain", "action_type": "kv.retain", "action_version": "1.0",
    "payload": {"scope": "session-id", "directives": [
      {"start": 0,    "end": 1200, "priority": 80, "duration": 86410},
      {"start": 1200, "end": null, "priority": 40, "duration": 86410}]}}]}}
```

- A directive protects the token range `[start, end)` of the prompt (`end: null` = to the end of the prompt, `covers_output: true` = the generated tail) with a priority 1–100 for `duration` seconds; priority 0 releases. Priorities must be non-increasing along the token axis (a later block is useless without its prefix).
- Protection is **soft**: the LRU free list is drained first, then protected blocks go lowest priority first; an expired protection is demoted to the LRU tail, not evicted. Hinted requests change the eviction *order*, never the capacity.
- A block keeps one hold per `scope` and is protected at the strongest hold; a scope only edits its own hold. `scope` is not authenticated (see `docs/usage/security.md`).
- With no hints the pool runs the upstream LRU path: retention bookkeeping starts with the first `kv.retain` of the process.

Commits:
1. `[Core] Add the kv.retain KV-hint action schema and parser` — `vllm/v1/kv_hints/retain.py`, strict (frontend) / lenient (engine) parsing, caps on actions and directives.
2. `[Frontend] Accept a kv_hints envelope on chat completions` — `ChatCompletionRequest.kv_hints`, validated, forwarded as request metadata; security note.
3. `[V1][Core] Priority-based KV-cache eviction driven by kv.retain hints` — `PriorityEvictionQueue` sidecar (lazy heap, expiry index) wired into `BlockPool`.
4. `[V1][Core] Drop a stale free copy when its hash is cached again` — an unreachable old copy no longer sits protected.
5. `[V1][Core] Keep one retention hold per scope and protect at the maximum` — per-scope holds; a scope lowering a block lowers its holds below it; orphaned descendants are reaped when the last copy of a hash leaves.
6. `[V1][Core] Link blocks into the hash chain only for full-attention KV groups` — the chain rules assume a lookup walks the chain from the first block; sliding-window and Mamba groups are left alone (keeps `test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector` green).
7. `[V1][Core] Keep the hint-free path at upstream cost until the first kv.retain hint` — see the microbenchmark below.

Out of scope here: hybrid/sliding-window specific retention (a follow-up), gRPC/Responses endpoints.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_hints tests/v1/core/test_priority_eviction.py \
       tests/tool_use/test_chat_completion_request_validations.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       "tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector" -q
pytest tests/v1/core -q          # CPU; compared against upstream/main in the same environment
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main..HEAD)
```

## Test Result

- 323 passed (the five suites above).
- `tests/v1/core` on a CPU-only box: the branch's failure set equals upstream/main's (read-only HF cache, no GPU: `test_kv_cache_utils` model-config downloads, `test_scheduler*` e2e). Before commit 6 the branch broke the two hybrid-Mamba cases; after it, none.
- pre-commit: all hooks pass (ruff check/format, mypy 3.10, typos, SPDX).

**What is compared.**

| column | server code | image | hints |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream LRU | upstream/main `189bbfb9` (the branch point; no retention code) | `base-189bbfb9-gfx90a` | none |
| branch LRU | this PR, commits 1–6 (`0b2ea132a6`, `0a6d417da9` after the rebase) | `base-0b2ea13-gfx90a` | none |
| branch + kv.retain | same code | same image | distance table |

Same client, session sets, KV size and send order in all three columns; the two LRU columns are byte-identical requests (no `retention_policy`). 2× MI250 (TP2), `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B`, ROCm images built from the commits above. +class TestReleaseRouting:
+    """A release must re-list only blocks it took out of the priority queue.
+
+    A free block can carry an entry while it is still linked on the LRU list
+    (an unpinned block, or any other path that leaves an entry on a block in
+    the LRU list). Appending it to the LRU list again corrupts the list: its
+    count drifts from its links, and allocation hands out the tail sentinel.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _manager_with_free_prefix():
+        block_size = 16
+        manager = make_kv_cache_manager(
+            make_kv_cache_config(block_size, 11),
+            max_model_len=8192,
+            enable_caching=True,
+            hash_block_size=block_size,
+        )
+        common = [i for i in range(3) for _ in range(block_size)]
+        request = make_request("p", common + [3] * 7, block_size, sha256)
+        computed, num_computed, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(request)
+        manager.allocate_slots(request, 55, num_computed, computed)
+        manager.free(request)
+        return manager, common
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _protect_then_release(manager, common):
+        pool = manager.block_pool
+        request = make_request("a", common + [3] * 5, 16, sha256)
+        computed, _, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(request)
+        (hit,) = computed.blocks
+        for priority in (75, 0):
+            pool._apply_retention_hook(
+                _HintedRequest([_d(start=0, end=48, priority=priority)], "s"),
+                list(hit),
+                len(hit),
+                16,
+            )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _walk(free_queue):
+        count, block = 0, free_queue.fake_free_list_head.next_free_block
+        seen: set[int] = set()
+        while block is not free_queue.fake_free_list_tail and block is not None:
+            assert block.block_id not in seen, "cycle in the free list"
+            seen.add(block.block_id)
+            count += 1
+            block = block.next_free_block
+        return count
+
+    def test_release_of_an_lru_listed_entry_keeps_the_list_consistent(self):
+        manager, common = self._manager_with_free_prefix()
+        self._protect_then_release(manager, common)
+
+        free_queue = manager.block_pool.free_block_queue
+        assert free_queue.num_free_blocks == self._walk(free_queue)
+
+    def test_allocation_after_such_a_release_returns_distinct_real_blocks(self):
+        manager, common = self._manager_with_free_prefix()

+
+        assert len(set(ids)) == len(ids) and all(i > 0 for i in ids), ids

+    """A block that is hit and freed over and over pushes a heap tuple per free;
+    only pop_lowest ever discards the stale ones. With allocations served from

+    skip through. The queue must compact on its own, and popping afterwards

+    assert queue.pop_lowest() is low

+"""The ``kv.retain`` KV-hint action: per-request retention directives for
+priority-based KV-cache eviction.
+
+Payload: ``{"scope": str | null, "directives": [directive, ...]}`` where a

+``{"covers_output": true, "priority", "duration"}``. Priority 1-100 protects
+the token range, 0 releases it; ranges no directive covers are left as they
+are. Priorities must be non-increasing along the token axis, because a
+prefix cache can only ever serve a block whose predecessors survived.

+from typing import Any, cast

+RETAIN_ACTION_TYPE = "kv.retain"
+RETAIN_ACTION_VERSION = "1.0"

+MAX_DURATION_S = 30 * 24 * 3600.0

+MAX_DIRECTIVES = 128

+    """One token range of a request and how strongly to keep its blocks.
+
+    ``end`` None means the end of the sequence, generated tokens included.
+    ``duration`` is seconds until the protection lapses, None for never. A
+    ``covers_output`` directive has no position of its own: the engine
+    resolves it to the generated tail once the prompt length is known.
+    """

+    priority: int
+    start: int = 0
+    end: int | None = None
+    duration: float | None = None
+    covers_output: bool = False

+    scope: str | None
+    directives: tuple[RetainDirective, ...]

+    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

+    if not isinstance(item, dict):
+        raise ValueError("each directive must be an object")
+    unknown = set(item) - _DIRECTIVE_FIELDS
+    if unknown:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown directive fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
+    priority_val = item.get("priority")
+    if not _is_int(priority_val):
+        raise ValueError(f"priority must be an integer in [0, {MAX_PRIORITY}]")
+    priority = cast(int, priority_val)
+    if not 0 <= priority <= MAX_PRIORITY:
+        raise ValueError(f"priority must be an integer in [0, {MAX_PRIORITY}]")

+    if not _is_int(start_val):
+        raise ValueError("start must be a non-negative integer")
+    start = cast(int, start_val)

+        raise ValueError("start must be a non-negative integer")
+    end_val = item.get("end")
+    if end_val is not None:
+        if not _is_int(end_val):
+            raise ValueError("end must be null or an integer greater than start")
+        end = cast(int, end_val)

+            raise ValueError("end must be null or an integer greater than start")

+        end = None
+    duration_val = item.get("duration")

I found a case where `kv.retain` updates are skipped for reused cache blocks. I've attached a proposed fix with regression tests.

**Reproducer**

For FA with a block size of 16:

1. A request populates a 64-token cached prefix and sets a hold with `scope="owner"`, `priority=50`, and `duration=30`.
2. A second request has the same 64-token prefix plus 2 additional tokens, and sends `priority=0` for the same scope.
3. It reuses the 64 cached tokens but finishes without publishing another full block. The old holds remain instead of being released.

Setting, renewing, and lowering holds are affected as well. If the continuation publishes a new full block, the existing publication hook applies the hints, so whether the update takes effect depends on crossing a block boundary.

**Proposed fix**

Apply the request's hints to adopted local FA/MLA full-block cache hits after successful allocation. This reuses the existing retention handler, preserving scope handling, TTL calculation, and descendant handling.

Failed admission does not update holds, and ordinary decode steps do not trigger this additional update. The existing publication path remains unchanged. This does not extend retention support to SWA/Mamba or partial checkpoints.

**Tests**

The patch adds `TestRetentionOnAdoptedCacheHits` to `tests/v1/core/test_priority_eviction.py`, covering set/renew/lower/release, failed admission, and decode without repeated renewal.

With only these tests added to the original implementation, five fail and one passes; with the fix, all six pass. The 262 existing tests in `test_priority_eviction.py` and `test_prefix_caching.py` also pass on both implementations. These were isolated component test runs, not full CI or real-model serving validation.

The attached patch is against `92b4241b1493d682e01ebd857110ce98a7781e02`. Does applying hints when cached blocks are adopted match your intended semantics? Happy to open a PR against your branch if that would be easier to review.

I noticed another case while testing this PR.

Suppose session A caches 64 tokens and asks to retain them for 100 seconds. Shortly afterward, session B sends the same 64 tokens without any retention hints. With 16-token blocks, vLLM reuses the first 48 tokens and recomputes the last block to get logits.

When that new block is cached, `_drop_stale_copies` removes the old copy, including A’s hold. The new copy can still serve a cache hit, but A’s protection is gone even though it hasn’t expired. If B sends 65 tokens instead, it reuses all four original blocks and A’s holds remain.

It looks like the cleanup assumes a duplicate was recomputed because the old prefix chain was broken, but normal last-block recomputation can also trigger it.

I’ve attached a small patch that carries the old copy’s unexpired holds over to the replacement before removing it. It keeps their original expiry times, then lets the current request’s hints apply as usual, so an explicit downgrade or release still works.

Does that match what you intended? My assumption is that A wants to retain the cached content, regardless of which physical block holds it. If holds are intentionally tied to individual physical copies, this would change that behavior.

One thing this patch leaves open is concurrent updates from the same scope: an older request can publish after a newer one, so publication order doesn’t necessarily reflect the latest intent. I haven’t added revision tracking here; do you think that should be handled separately?

The patch includes 10 tests. Those and the 262 existing cache-component tests pass with the fix. I haven’t run real-model serving validation yet. This is separate from the earlier cache-hit fix and can be applied on its own.
